title: 502 Bad Gateway
description: Fix 502 errors when the web server cannot get a valid response from PHP-FPM or upstream services.

steps.title: Confirm Scope and Timing
steps.instructions: Check if the 502 affects the whole site or specific URLs. Note when it started — often tied to deploys, traffic spikes, or host maintenance.

steps.title: Check Host Status and Resource Limits
steps.instructions: Review hosting dashboard for CPU, memory, or connection limit alerts. Restart PHP-FPM or the web server pool if your host allows it.

steps.title: Review PHP-FPM and Nginx/Apache Logs
steps.instructions: Look for 'upstream timed out', 'connection refused', or 'pool exhausted' messages. Increase pm.max_children or worker limits with your host if pools are saturated.

steps.title: Identify Long-Running PHP Scripts
steps.instructions: Heavy imports, backup plugins, or cron jobs can tie up workers. Pause large jobs, run them via WP-CLI or off-peak, and add object caching if queries are slow.

steps.title: Check CDN or Reverse Proxy
steps.instructions: If using Cloudflare or a load balancer, confirm origin server health and SSL mode. Purge CDN cache and verify origin responds directly by IP or bypass rule.

steps.title: Temporarily Disable Heavy Plugins
steps.instructions: Deactivate caching, security scanners, or backup plugins that hook early. Re-enable after confirming the origin responds within gateway timeout limits.

steps.title: Monitor After Stabilization
steps.instructions: Watch response times and error rate for 24–48 hours. Document root cause and any host configuration changes for future incidents.
